texts: In Carpentier's functional classification, type IIIb, restricted leaflet motion in systole, is the classic ischaemic mitral regurgitation: E.
After a heart attack, the stag shot by an arrow, the floor of the ventricle sags and pulls the chords down, so the leaflets are tethered and cannot close in systole.
Type I has normal leaflet motion, with a widened annulus or a hole; type II has excessive motion, prolapse or a flail, the sail.
Type IIIa is restricted in both systole and diastole, as in rheumatic disease, the scarlet beads.
Memory hook: the carpenter drops the mitre with the pulled-down strings into the bin IIIb.
